paper.title: Prompt a Robot to Walk with Large Language Models
paper.central_claim: Frozen GPT-4 directly produces low-level walking joint targets from normalized historical observations/actions and control descriptions, without task-specific LLM finetuning, across robots/terrains/simulators.

evidence.quote: We do one-time initialization of the prompt based on an existing controller, which could be either model-based or learning-based.
evidence.support_explanation: Existing-controller behavior initializes the LLM context; no data-free gait learning.

evidence.quote: we use a linear transformation to map all the potential numeric values into non-negative integers ranging from 0 to 200
The LLM outputs normalized target joint positions that are then tracked by a PD controller.
evidence.support_explanation: Continuous targets plus external tracking; not semantic skill selection.

evidence.quote: each trial lasts for 10 seconds, and we have 5 trials for each experiment.
evidence.support_explanation: Counted description-prompt trials with defined horizon; not denominators for every experiment.

evidence.quote: only actions were provided, which essentially amounts to an open-loop control. This form of control was insufficient for successfully making the robot walk
evidence.support_explanation: Open-loop ablation supports feedback dependence, not physical-understanding inference.

evidence.quote: Following the same approach, we train a 10 Hz RL policy for initialization.
evidence.support_explanation: Separate ANYmal initializer; not direct transfer of a single policy/context.

evidence.quote: our prompt design inevitably becomes biased toward this policy.
evidence.support_explanation: Prompt-development dependence on behavior policy explicitly admitted.

evidence.quote: we have to pause the simulation to wait for the output of GPT-4.
evidence.support_explanation: 10Hz means simulated control time, not actual real-time capability.

evidence.quote: roughly costed \$2,000 US dollars for all the OpenAI API calls.
evidence.support_explanation: Aggregate API price, not per-setting runtime/failed-run price.
Readable normalization table has conflicting percent header and fractional-looking values. Preserve ambiguity.

signatures.object: Frozen text LLM walking feedback policy
signatures.information: Proprioceptive/sensor values and action history; RL/model-based controller initializer; descriptions of joint order, control and task.
signatures.operation: Map numerical inputs/targets to 0–200 integers, condition GPT-4 on 50-step history, denormalize targets, track with PD and append next actual observation.
signatures.output: Joint-position target at 10Hz simulated update rate; PD 200Hz
signatures.conditions: Simulator pauses during inference; robot-specific suitable initializer and fragile prompt.
signatures.feedback: Next actual sensor state/action enters sliding history.
signatures.selection_rule: Latest history replaces initializer; no candidate acceptance, verifier or harness optimizer.
signatures.selection_data: Current episode plus designer-provided few-shot/initializer data; no automatically retained harness changes.
signatures.persistence: Episode context only; frozen LLM and fixed designer schema.
signatures.failure_boundary: No real-time physical deployment; initialization bias, prompt fragility, missing full cross-robot counts.

gap.author_gap: LLMs typically do high-level planning or need robot-specific training; test whether a frozen language model can directly drive dynamic feedback walking.
gap.checked_gap: Low-level numerical interface is a concrete residual distinct from high-level reward/contact planning; independent fulltexts of neighbors not supplied.

claims.text: Frozen GPT-4 functions as dynamic walking feedback controller.
claims.setting: A1/MuJoCo, 10Hz simulated target updates with PD 200Hz.
claims.selection_vs_test: Prompt developed using particular RL initializer; no separate tuning/test episodes.
claims.result/denominator: Five trials/10-second description study; Table I extends to 20 seconds: NWT .137/.086/.700/.504/.721, success entries 0/0/.6/.2/.6 with ambiguous [%] label.
claims.counterevidence: Trajectory divergence from RL does not isolate physics understanding; simulation paused; table-unit ambiguity retained.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Feasibility of this short simulated feedback pipeline, not gait learning from text alone.

claims.counterevidence: Initializer retraining and unknown counts prevent transfer-level classification.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Recipe instantiated on two simulated robots; no counted transfer or real-time physical success.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Authors report short-horizon simulated closed-loop walking from a frozen GPT-4 numerical-history prompt, controller-derived initializer and PD tracking; counted prompt ablations support feasibility, not real-time or count-based cross-embodiment transfer.
